en.name: Augustine of Hippo
en.summary: Bishop of Hippo and Doctor of the Church whose Confessions and City of God shaped Western Christian thought for over a millennium.
en.body: Augustine spent much of his youth pursuing worldly ambition and philosophical wandering before his conversion in Milan in 386, an experience he recounts in his Confessions — one of the first and most influential works of Western autobiography. As bishop of Hippo Regius in North Africa, he wrote prolifically on grace, free will, and the nature of the Church, and his City of God, composed after the sack of Rome in 410, wrestled with the relationship between the earthly and heavenly cities. His theology remains foundational to both Catholic and Protestant thought.
